text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.3% today to $152.02, extending a two-week gain of 3.76%. The climb follows major earnings beats from Chevron and Exxon yesterday, driven by soaring refining profits—diesel prices have surged globally because Ukraine and Iran have damaged Russian and Middle Eastern refineries, tightening fuel supply. As a major refiner itself, ConocoPhillips benefits directly from these wider margins between crude costs and refined product prices.

The broader tailwind is geopolitical volatility in oil-producing regions: Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure, reported Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian refineries, and fresh tensions in the Strait of Hormuz (where Iran claims tankers hit mines) are all keeping energy markets tight and refining economics favorable. This fits a pattern where conflict-driven supply disruptions are lifting the entire big oil sector's profitability.
